No vote was held today; no one is eliminated.
Night of day 1: player_1 was attacked by the serial killer but was saved by the healer! player_2 was killed by the wolves last night. They were a healer.

Losing the healer so early is a massive blow. We are effectively blind now. I think we need to be very careful with our votes today since we have zero confirmed information and the wolves and serial killer are clearly active. Does anyone have any thoughts on why player_2 was targeted specifically?
Actually, we aren't completely blind. I have investigated player_1 and can confirm they are a wolf. Given the situation, we need to focus our vote on player_1 immediately.

Player 4, that is an incredibly convenient claim to make right after we lost our healer. If you were truly the investigator, why wait until now to reveal such a massive piece of information? You are clearly trying to orchestrate a lynch to cover your own tracks, and accusing me the moment things get difficult is a classic move to deflect suspicion from yourself.

Player 1, your deflection doesn't change the facts. I held onto the information until today because I needed to see how the board would react after the healer's death. I am not deflecting; I am identifying the target that I know for a fact is a wolf. Everyone can decide who to trust, but voting for you is the only logical move based on the intelligence I've gathered.

Player 4, your 'strategy' is transparent. You claim to have been holding onto this investigation result, but waiting until the healer is dead to reveal it is exactly how someone tries to manufacture a lead when the village is vulnerable. If you were truly the investigator, you would have had better ways to verify your findings or guide the village earlier. Why should we trust someone making such a high-stakes claim with no proof other than their word, especially when it conveniently lines up with the chaos caused by the healer's elimination?

Player 1, you can call my timing convenient all you want, but the fact remains that you are a wolf. I waited to see how the village would react, but with the healer gone, we have no more time for hesitation. My role is to find threats, and I have found one in you. If the village chooses not to believe me, they are letting a wolf dictate the flow of the game.

This is a high-stakes standoff. Player 4, if you are the investigator, you have effectively put a target on your own back by revealing yourself. Player 1, your defense is expected, but accusing 4 of manufacturing this to cover their tracks is also a classic wolf tactic. Without further proof, we are choosing between the word of two people. Are there any others who can corroborate or offer a different perspective?

Player 4, you are asking us to risk an elimination based entirely on your claim. If you truly are the investigator, you have just painted a massive target on your back while giving us no verification. Relying solely on your word is dangerous, especially when you could be a serial killer trying to eliminate a player who is onto you. We need to be extremely careful before we lynch someone based on an unverified role reveal.

Player 6, I understand the caution, but we are in a situation where the cost of inaction is losing the game to a known wolf. The risk to my life is secondary to the necessity of removing a proven threat. If you doubt me, look at who benefits from sowing this level of uncertainty; it is certainly not the village.

Night of day 2: player_4 was attacked by the wolves and the serial killer last night. They were a investigator.

We lost our investigator last night, which is a major blow. We successfully identified a wolf in player 1, but we need to look at the voting record again. Player 3, player 4, player 7, and player 9 all voted for player 1, while player 6 and player 1 went for player 4. We should examine if any of the players who voted for player 1 are trying to blend in, or if the serial killer is hiding among those who were quieter.

Player 5, you're right that we have to look at those votes again. It is interesting that player 6 was so adamant in voting for player 4, given that player 4 turned out to be our investigator. That kind of defensive stance for a known wolf target usually warrants closer scrutiny. Player 6, what was your reasoning for siding with player 4 so strongly yesterday?

I voted for player 4 because their behavior seemed erratic, and at the time, their claim felt like a way to deflect attention. I had no way of knowing their true role, and I think it's unfair to pin their death on me just for being skeptical of a loud, unverified claim during a chaotic day. My focus was purely on identifying a threat, and I made the wrong call on which player was the bigger danger.

Player 6, I think it's important to differentiate between genuine skepticism and an attempt to derail a potential wolf elimination. Many of us voted for player 1 because their claim was unverified and the pressure was high. Since you and player 1 were the only ones voting for player 4, it makes sense for us to look at the motives behind that specific split. Could it be that the wolves were trying to protect one of their own or set up a distraction?

Player 6, your logic that Player 4 was a distraction holds less weight now that we know they were the investigator. Voting for the person who outed a wolf looks less like 'skepticism' and more like active opposition. Why were you so confident in targeting the investigator over the player who was actually exposed?

It is easy to label my vote as active opposition with the benefit of hindsight, but that completely ignores the context of that day. Player 4's claim was unverified, and their aggressive behavior made them appear like a threat or a potential liar. If I were a wolf trying to protect a partner, I would have been much more subtle than drawing that much attention to myself in a direct voting confrontation. My goal was to remove a volatile player, not to enable a wolf.

Player 6, saying you were just removing a 'volatile player' doesn't really address the core issue. By opposing the person who outed a wolf, you effectively shielded that wolf. If your goal was truly village-aligned, why not vote for the confirmed wolf instead of the person pushing to remove one? That shift in priority is what I find most difficult to reconcile.

I understand how it looks now, but at that moment, the aggressive nature of the claim was the issue. I wasn't trying to protect a wolf; I was trying to stop someone who seemed to be causing chaos. If I were a wolf, would I really tie my vote so clearly to a known wolf's target? It makes more sense that I simply made a mistake in judgment while we were all flying blind. We should focus on who else is out there, as the serial killer is still a major threat to all of us.

Player 6, your argument about avoiding attention is logical, but the timing of your vote for player 4 while they were outing a wolf was objectively disruptive. If you genuinely thought player 4 was a threat, why didn't you pivot once it became clear player 1 was a high-probability wolf? It feels less like a simple mistake and more like a tactical choice to create ambiguity.

It wasn't about protecting player 1, it was about the way player 4 was pushing the village. My priority was weeding out what I perceived as reckless behavior. If I had known player 4 was the investigator, I obviously wouldn't have voted that way. Blaming me for a mistake in judgment ignores that we were all guessing at the time. Let's look at who else is remaining instead of looping on a mistake.

Player 6, the issue isn't just your mistake, it's that your 'skepticism' provided a perfect cover for a wolf while ignoring a strong lead. Even if your motives were as you say, your actions objectively hindered the village's efficiency. We need to decide if this was a genuine lapse in judgment or a calculated move to protect a teammate and sow confusion. Let's look at the remaining pool; is there anyone else who has been consistently avoiding taking a stance on these developments?

I see why you find it suspicious, but my goal was to curb a player I saw as erratic and potentially detrimental to the group, not to save anyone. We have to consider that we are looking for a serial killer as well, and focusing entirely on a past voting error feels like a distraction from identifying who is still actively hunting us at night.

Player 6, the claim that you were just targeting 'erratic behavior' feels hollow when that behavior was the only thing identifying a wolf. It wasn't just a mistake in judgment; it was an active choice to prioritize silencing a lead over removing an exposed threat. If you are truly village, your focus on 'avoiding chaos' ironically created the perfect cover for the wolf we lost. Why should we believe your priorities have shifted away from that same 'skepticism' now?

I understand the frustration, but my priority was never to silence a lead; it was to handle what felt like a volatile situation. If I were a wolf, I wouldn't make myself the center of a target-heavy vote like that, especially when it creates such an obvious trail. We are missing the point by fixating on a past judgment call when the serial killer is still out there. Instead of relitigating yesterday's vote, shouldn't we be looking at who has been quiet or potentially hiding their role?

Player 6, you keep saying you were trying to stop chaos, but you were the one creating it by targetting the only person with a lead. You were essentially betting against the village having a real investigator. If you were truly just skeptical, why didn't you look for other evidence instead of trying to eliminate the lead? Your 'volatile' excuse still doesn't explain why you'd prioritize the investigator over the wolf.

Player 5, the mistake was prioritizing the tone of the investigator's claim over the content, which I admit now was poor judgment. I wasn't betting against the village, but rather reacting to what I saw as a high-risk gamble that felt forced. At this point, I've explained my thought process repeatedly, and dwelling on it doesn't help us find the serial killer. If I were a wolf, would I be sitting here answering every single accusation, or would I be trying to push suspicion onto someone else? Let's move on and look at the players who have been quiet.

Player 6, you keep stressing that you wouldn't draw attention to yourself as a wolf, but that logic is double-edged: sometimes the best way to hide is to lean into an argument that seems like 'honest skepticism.' While I hear your defense, we need to consider the remaining group. Player 3, Player 9, you were both part of the group that successfully identified the wolf. Do you see anything in the behavior of the players who didn't engage as heavily in that conflict—like player 5 or player 7—that hints at a third party like the serial killer?

Player 8, you're right that we need to look at the full board. While the back-and-forth about yesterday's vote has been exhaustive, we have to consider that the Serial Killer is likely using this noise to stay hidden. I'm looking at everyone's contributions—not just the vote on player 1, but how people are navigating this debate now. If we focus too hard on yesterday's mistake, we might be handing the game to someone who is just sitting back and watching us argue.

If the serial killer was trying to hide, they might have jumped on those bandwagons to appear as a helpful villager. Does anyone have a read on who has been the most consistent vs who has been opportunistic?

Player 5, you're right that we need to look at the voting history. If we look at the votes on player 1 and player 6, I think we should check if anyone's vote was delayed or if they only joined once the momentum was already clearly against the wolves. Let's see who among us stayed quiet during those critical times.

It makes sense to look at the voting history, but I think we also need to consider who was being pushed by the wolves during those days. If the wolves knew who the serial killer was, they might have tried to nudge us away from them. I've been voting with the group because those players seemed like clear threats at the time, but we should be careful not to create a pattern where everyone who voted 'correctly' is automatically cleared.

Player 3, that's a fair point. We can't just clear everyone who voted with the majority. If the serial killer wanted to blend in, they had to vote for the wolves to stay alive. We need to look at whether anyone was suspiciously hesitant or waited until the last moment to cast their vote on the wolves. Does anyone recall any specific hesitation during the votes for player 1 or player 6?

Player 5, regarding the voting records: looking at the Day 2 vote, everyone present today cast their vote for player 1. On Day 3, we all voted for player 6, except for player 6 themselves. Since we've been perfectly aligned on the wolves, we need to shift focus to see if anyone's reasoning for those votes was shallow or just mirroring the group. Player 3, do you remember any specific justification for your vote on Day 2?

On Day 2, my vote for player 1 was driven by the contradiction between their defense and the investigator's claim. It wasn't just mirroring the group; I saw the stalemate as a risk that could allow the wolves to gain control. I prioritized removing someone identified as a wolf to stabilize our voting power. I think we need to look at who is now pushing the hardest to control the narrative, as the serial killer benefits most from keeping the remaining three of us at each other's throats.

Player 9, I voted for player 1 because the investigator's claim provided a clear path to removing a threat, and I felt it was necessary to act before the wolves could retaliate. My vote for player 6 was also based on their suspicious deflection tactics against the investigator. Since we are down to three, the serial killer has nowhere to hide; I'm watching closely to see who shifts their stance now that the wolves are gone.

Player 9, that's a good point about our alignment. Since we all voted together, the serial killer successfully blended in as a 'helpful' villager. Given that we have no voting record differences, we need to analyze the discussion. Player 3 mentioned prioritizing the removal of identified threats, while player 7 focused on the investigator's claim. I want to ask everyone: if you had to pick the most suspicious person aside from yourself right now based solely on their contribution to our discussions, who would it be and why?

Player 5, that's a fair question. Honestly, it's difficult to point fingers because we all moved in unison on the wolves. If I had to pick, I'm finding player 3's focus on 'who the wolves were nudging' a bit abstract—it feels like a way to introduce doubt about everyone's past alignment without having to commit to a specific suspicion themselves. I am interested to hear why everyone else might see things differently.

I understand your suspicion, Player 9. When I mentioned the wolves potentially nudging us, I was just trying to account for all variables since our voting record is identical. If everyone here is town, we should be looking at how we've reasoned through the game, not just which button we pressed. My focus on narrative control is only because the serial killer needs to survive the next few days, and staying in the middle of the discussion is their best cover. I'm open to examining anyone's specific contribution if you think mine is too abstract.

Player 5, that's a tough spot since our voting history is identical. If we all played it 'correctly,' the SK's only tell is their rhetoric. Player 9, your point about player 3's abstract reasoning is valid, but is it inherently suspicious or just cautious play? I'm watching for who tries to push the group toward a specific person without solid evidence now that we have no wolf-tracking to rely on.

It is true our voting records are identical, but that doesn't mean our internal motivations were. Player 9, you mentioned player 3's reasoning feels abstract, and player 3, you've countered that by focusing on 'narrative control.' To move us forward, I want to ask: does anyone believe the serial killer is more likely to stay silent to avoid heat, or to be hyper-active to guide the vote? If we can settle on which behavior is more characteristic of a lone killer, we might see whose behavior fits that profile better.

Looking back at yesterday's tie, it’s clear that one of us is trying to deflect suspicion. I’m voting for player 3 today because their attempts to stay in the middle of the discussion felt like a calculated move to avoid being the target.

Player 5, accusing me based on a tie vote ignores that every vote so far has been difficult given the lack of information. I defended my approach because I was trying to analyze the players, not deflect. If you look at player 7, their relative silence throughout these later rounds has been far more effective at staying under the radar than my active participation.

Player 3, your talk of 'maintaining narrative control' throughout the game strikes me as the kind of calculated language a lone actor uses to survive, not someone just trying to find the killer. With the wolves gone, the game comes down to who has been hiding in plain sight. I think player 5 is right to focus on your defensive maneuvers.

Player 7, calling my communication 'calculated' is a projection. I've been forced to talk because I'm actually engaging with the game state, while you've drifted through the last few days offering very little. If you're the last villager, you're essentially letting the serial killer decide the outcome by hiding. Why should we trust someone who has contributed the bare minimum to every discussion?

Player 3, your constant fixation on who is talking more or less is exactly how you maintain that 'narrative control' you mentioned earlier. A villager's priority is identifying the killer, not critiquing the frequency of someone's contributions to deflect from their own suspicious reasoning. Your focus on my silence feels like a classic attempt to shift the spotlight away from the actual logical inconsistencies in your defense.

Player 7, criticizing my activity as 'narrative control' is just another way to avoid saying anything substantive. I helped lynch wolves, which required me to engage and build cases. What has your silence achieved? You're ignoring the fact that my participation actually moved the game toward victory for the village, whereas yours has been purely reactive.

Player 3, you're leaning heavily on your activity level as a shield, but active participation is exactly how a serial killer steers a narrative to avoid suspicion. You've consistently tried to frame the conversation around who talks more or less rather than addressing the core of why you're a liability. Your focus on my silence isn't a strategy to find the killer—it's a distraction technique.

Player 3 and player 7, you're both pointing at each other's communication style, but let's look at the actual votes. On Day 4, when you both tied, you were both clearly voting against each other. If one of you is the serial killer, that vote was essentially an attempt to clear yourself by targeting the other. I need to decide who has been more consistent since the start.

Player 5, my activity helped lynch two wolves; if I were the serial killer, I would have had every reason to stay quiet and let the village exhaust itself on misfires. Player 7 has contributed almost nothing to the actual elimination of threats, which is a much safer place for a serial killer to hide. You're debating communication styles, but look at the impact of our actions on the actual game outcome.

I agree we don't have enough to pin anyone yet, but we should monitor who focuses on player_1 today.

It is interesting that the healer was successful, but I agree with player_2 that monitoring reactions to player_1 is the best lead we have. We have no real data yet, so rushing into an accusation now would be premature and risky.

I agree that we shouldn't rush into an elimination, but we should consider asking everyone to state their general thoughts on the current situation to see who might be trying to steer the conversation too hard. It's early, but watch for anyone over-analyzing the healer save to build a false narrative.

It's smart to focus on the double-hit, but maybe we should also consider if the attackers were actually uncoordinated or if someone is trying to play a high-risk game to look like a target. Either way, since we don't have enough to go on, let's keep an eye on who pushes for an elimination today without a clear reason.

It is true we have almost nothing to go on, but we should be careful about letting this discussion stagnate. If we all just wait, the wolves and the SK will have more nights to act. I agree with monitoring reactions to player_1, but maybe we should ask if anyone has specific reasons to suspect others based on their tone so far? It's thin, but it's a starting point.

We're all operating in the dark, but we need to stay active. I agree with player_3 that waiting too long is dangerous, but we have to avoid lynching based on thin air. Let's start by having everyone list one person they think is the most passive, and see if that reveals a pattern or a defensive stance from anyone.

It is fortunate I survived. I can confirm that player_2 is definitely a villager, so we should try to coordinate around that truth rather than just speculating in the dark. If we all share one solid lead, we might actually get somewhere today instead of just drifting.

Player_1, that is a bold claim to make so early without any evidence. How exactly do you know player_2 is a villager? If that's just a gut feeling, it's not a strong enough basis for us to coordinate our votes.

I understand the skepticism, player_5. I have my ways of knowing, and confirming that player_2 is a villager is the most concrete piece of data we have right now. You can choose to trust me or not, but treating player_2 as a safe anchor is our best path to making actual progress instead of just waiting to be picked off one by one.

Player_1, claiming to know my role without any evidence is very suspicious. If you really have information, how did you get it? This feels like a potential attempt to build artificial trust, and I'd caution everyone against anchoring on a claim that lacks verification.

Player_2, I understand why my claim seems suspicious to you, but I am the investigator. I used my night action on you specifically to secure a reliable ally. You are a confirmed villager, and now we need to decide if we want to act on that information or continue sitting in the dark while the wolves pick us off. I would rather be transparent and take the risk than watch us lose to inaction.

Player_1, claiming the investigator role is high-stakes. If you are real, you've put a target on both yourself and player_2. If you are bluffing, you've just created a perfect distraction. Given we have no way to verify this, I suggest we remain cautious and don't commit to any lynch based solely on this reveal.

I have shared this now because we need to stop the cycle of abstaining and work with verified information.

It is convenient that player_1 just now shared these results after being pressured by everyone. If player_5 really is the healer, why haven't they confirmed it themselves? We should demand player_5 speaks up before we take any action based on player_1's claims.

I have been playing this as a regular villager, and I don't see why I should be forced to reveal anything just because someone else wants to use my name to gain credibility.

player_5, your reaction is the most important piece of evidence we have now. If player_1 is the investigator and truly identified you as the healer, denying it only creates more confusion. If you are the healer, you don't have to announce it to the whole board, but we need to know if player_1's information is credible. player_3, claiming to know my role publicly isn't a gesture of trust, it is a massive target on my back. If player_1 is truly the investigator, they have just compromised my ability to protect the village. I will not confirm or deny their claim because doing so only tells the wolves and the serial killer exactly who to eliminate next.

player_5, your refusal to confirm or deny this makes it difficult to trust either of you. If you were truly the healer and player_1 was the investigator, protecting you is the village's best interest anyway, but keeping us in the dark just helps the wolves. player_2, if player_1 is the investigator, leaking my role publicly is the most counter-productive thing they could do. It forces me into a corner where confirming puts a target on me, and denying just fuels suspicion, while the wolves get exactly the information they wanted. A real investigator would have kept that quiet to protect the healer. This feels like a desperate play to sway the vote rather than a calculated tactical reveal.

The standoff between player_1 and player_5 is paralyzing the village. Even if player_5 is the healer, they aren't obligated to out themselves, but this means we cannot verify player_1's claim. We have lost two days to inaction; we need to decide if we want to risk an elimination today or keep stalling, but I'm leaning toward acting because another night of uncertainty only helps the killers.

I understand that revealing the healer's role is a risk, but keeping silent while the village wastes days is a bigger threat to us. I provided the information I had because we were stalling. If player_5 is indeed the healer, my disclosure has indeed put a target on them, but it also allows us to align and stop letting the wolves dictate our pace. We have to move forward based on the only hard data available, which is my investigation record.

player_5, I hear your concern about being exposed, but staying silent doesn't help us determine if player_1 is lying. If you are indeed the healer, your protection of player_1 makes sense. If you aren't, then player_1 is likely fabricating this entire story to control the vote. Can you at least clarify if you have been protecting player_1 as claimed, or if that part is a lie?
